title: Grimm's Waxworks
victim: Oswald Grimm, owner of the waxworks
teaser: Grimm promised the guests at the night viewing a new figure nobody had seen yet. The new figure turned up in the Chamber of Horrors: Grimm himself in the executioner's chair, with a brass plaque at his feet bearing his name and today's date. The plaque was ordered from the engraver in advance, and everyone who has worked even a day in the museum smells of wax and turpentine.
locations: The boiler room with the wax vats

habits.label: Executioner's hood
habits.habit: A black canvas executioner's hood with eyeholes
clues: In the Chamber of Horrors a black canvas thread is caught on the arm of the executioner's chair, yet the hood on the wax executioner is intact. The culprit has an executioner's hood.
In the store of old figures the hood has been taken off a retired executioner, leaving a clean patch on the figure's dusty shoulders. The culprit wears a black executioner's hood.

habits.label: Skull make-up
habits.habit: Face made up as a skull: white greasepaint and soot
clues: The glass of the axe display in the Chamber of Horrors has the print of a forehead and cheekbone: white greasepaint, with black soot round the eye sockets. The culprit has skull make-up on.
In the ticket hall the mirror by the coat rack has a white cheek mark and black smudges of soot. The culprit's face is made up as a skull.

habits.label: Tin lantern
habits.habit: Carries a tin lantern with a candle stub inside
clues: In the store of old figures a line of round marks from the base of a lantern runs through the dust, as if it was set down by every figure. The culprit carries a tin lantern.
In the boiler room by the wax vats lies a wire handle from a tin lantern, the break still shiny. The culprit has a tin lantern with a candle.

habits.label: Pumpkin seeds
clues: In the owner's office there are white pumpkin seed husks under the desk, and Grimm fined people for litter on the floor. The culprit nibbles pumpkin seeds.
In the sculptor's workshop a pumpkin seed is pressed into the soft wax of an unfinished hand. The culprit has pumpkin seeds in their pocket.

habits.label: Bat in the buttonhole
habits.habit: A paper bat in their buttonhole
clues: In the Hall of Kings a black paper wing with a pinhole lies at the feet of Henry VIII. The culprit has a paper bat in their buttonhole.
In the boiler room a pin with a scrap of black paper cut into a wing glints on the coal heap. The culprit wears a paper bat in their buttonhole.

habits.label: Rubber spider
habits.habit: Carries a rubber spider in their pocket for jokes
clues: In the owner's office a rubber spider sits on the papers for the sale of the museum, and Grimm couldn't stand jokes with props. The culprit carries a rubber spider in their pocket.
A guest at the viewing screamed in the Hall of Kings: someone threw a rubber spider onto her glove from behind the velvet rope. The culprit has a rubber spider in their pocket.

habits.label: Glass eye
habits.habit: A glass eye in their pocket as a lucky charm
clues: In the Hall of Kings a brown glass eye has rolled under the velvet rope, and all the kings have blue eyes. The culprit has a glass eye in their pocket.
The cleaner saw someone in the ticket hall rolling a glass eye between their fingers like prayer beads. The culprit carries a glass eye as a lucky charm.

habits.label: Plaster on the cuffs
clues: The black velvet of the executioner's chair in the Chamber of Horrors has white streaks of plaster dust, as if from a sleeve. The culprit has plaster on their cuffs.
In the ticket hall the dark cash desk has a white sleeve mark, and it's plaster, not chalk. The culprit has plaster dust on their cuffs.

habits.label: Gold tooth
habits.habit: A gold tooth at the side that flashes when they smile
clues: A guest at the viewing remembered someone's smile in the half-dark of the Hall of Kings with a gold tooth flashing in it. The culprit has a gold tooth.
Grimm's diary in the owner's office has an entry for today: "22:00, Gold Tooth, final talk." The culprit has a gold tooth.

habits.label: Owl cane
habits.habit: A cane with an owl-shaped handle
clues: In the sculptor's workshop a soft wax blank bears a clear impression of the owl's head from a cane handle. The culprit has a cane with an owl handle.
In the store of old figures, round holes from the tip of a cane run beside the shoe prints. The culprit walks with a cane.

habits.label: Mint pastilles
habits.habit: Sucks mint pastilles for their throat
clues: In the Chamber of Horrors, which smells only of wax, a cool smell of mint lingers over the executioner's chair. The culprit smells of mint pastilles.
An empty tin of mint pastilles lies by the furnace in the boiler room, its lid still smelling of mint. The culprit sucks mint pastilles.

habits.label: Loupe on a chain
habits.habit: A jeweller's loupe on a chain
clues: On the table of plaster moulds in the sculptor's workshop lies a broken chain with the brass ring from a jeweller's loupe. The culprit wears a loupe on a chain.
In the store of old figures the dust by a wax queen's eye has been wiped away in a neat circle, as if by the rim of a loupe. The culprit has a jeweller's loupe on a chain.

habits.label: Anchor tattoo
habits.habit: A blue anchor tattooed on their hand
clues: The fireman on duty at the viewing saw a hand with a blue anchor on it by the executioner's chair in the Chamber of Horrors and took it for wax. The culprit has an anchor tattoo.
The engraver's errand boy remembered only the hand that slipped him a tip in the ticket hall: it had a blue anchor on it. The culprit has an anchor tattooed on their hand.

habits.label: Brilliantine in the hair
clues: In the owner's office the high back of the chair has a greasy patch with a sharp smell of brilliantine, and Grimm is completely bald. The culprit uses brilliantine.
In the sculptor's workshop the wig comb has a greasy film of brilliantine, and the wigs there are combed dry. The culprit has brilliantine in their hair.

habits.label: Petrol lighter
clues: In the store of old figures a finger on a wax hand is melted, and there's a smell of petrol nearby, like from a lighter. The culprit carries a petrol lighter.
A guest at the viewing heard the dry click of a lighter lid in the dark Hall of Kings and smelled petrol. The culprit has a petrol lighter.

habits.label: Cotton gloves
habits.habit: White cotton gloves in any weather
clues: In the sculptor's workshop white cotton fluff is stuck to the fresh varnish of the new figure. The culprit wears white cotton gloves.
A charred finger from a white cotton glove lies in the ash by the furnace in the boiler room. The culprit has white cotton gloves.

tools: The executioner's chair in the Chamber of Horrors was unscrewed from the platform and screwed back, the screws driven fully home. The culprit is handy with tools.
The brass plaque at Grimm's feet is fixed to its stand with four small nails exactly on the marks, and the soft brass hasn't a single dent. The culprit is handy with tools.
french: "Fin de la collection", French for "End of the collection", is scratched on the back of the brass plaque in the Chamber of Horrors. The culprit knows French.
In the owner's office the contract with the museum's Paris buyer lies open, and an error in one French clause has been corrected in pencil. The culprit knows French.
strong: The heavy Grimm was sat in the executioner's chair, yet the parquet in the Chamber of Horrors hasn't a single streak: he was carried. The culprit is physically strong.
In the store of old figures the cabinet of plaster moulds, which removal men shift in pairs, has been pushed aside. The culprit is physically strong.
medic: In the owner's office an unfinished glass of cognac smells of bitter almonds, and the decanter beside it has been rinsed. The culprit knows about poisons.
A jar of arsenic green for paints is missing from the cupboard in the sculptor's workshop, with exactly a teaspoonful taken out. The culprit knows about poisons.
quiet: The old parquet in the Hall of Kings creaks at every step, yet the guests at the ropes heard nobody behind them. The culprit moves silently.
The door of the owner's office squeals on its hinges down the whole corridor, yet Grimm never looked up from his papers. The culprit moves silently.
passages: An old coal chute behind the figure of Jack the Ripper leads from the boiler room to the Chamber of Horrors, and the soot has been wiped off its hatch. The culprit knows the service passages.
The store of old figures is connected to the sculptor's workshop by a lift for mannequins, and the car isn't on its usual floor. The culprit knows the service passages.
cash: The night viewing's takings are gone from the till in the ticket hall, yet the cash book balances to the penny. The culprit had access to money.
The engraver was paid in advance for the plaque from an envelope with the museum's seal, the kind only wages are paid in. The culprit had access to money.
sched: It all happened in the ten minutes when, according to the programme, the tour stands in the Hall of Kings hearing about Henry VIII's six wives. The culprit knows the schedule.
At ten in the evening the boiler room lets off steam on schedule, and for a quarter of an hour the roar in the pipes drowns every sound in the Chamber of Horrors. The culprit knows the schedule.
keys: The Chamber of Horrors grille is locked during viewings, yet it was opened with a key, the lock unscratched. The culprit had keys.
The store of old figures is locked at night, but the padlock was taken off and neatly hung back on its hasp. The culprit had keys.
tech: The light in the Chamber of Horrors went out for exactly a minute: a fuse in the box was unscrewed, then put back. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The mechanical queen in the Hall of Kings who turns her head to the guests was stopped by removing one wire from her little motor. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
safe: The fireproof safe in the owner's office was opened with the combination, and an IOU in Grimm's name is missing from it. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The takings safe in the ticket hall was opened without a single scratch, and the museum's insurance policy isn't inside. The culprit knows the safe combination.
